capabilities: Set up GTD folders, overview notes, and a Weekly Review checklist
Capture items or selected text as notes in the Inbox folder
Two-way sync note changes with a GTD Brain board
Regenerate Next Actions by context and project overview notes
Sign in with an email code and manage sync settings
extras: The plugin is free and MIT-licensed, but any sync in either direction requires a paid GTD Brain membership; without it notes stay local and nothing syncs. Requests are logged server-side by GTD Brain's backend (endpoint, timestamp, per-install id, version, account), though the plugin has no client-side telemetry. The manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in GTD workflow, and notes in a vault normally stay separate from the same task list available on the web, phones, and AI assistants.

relations.evidence: The plugin is a client for GTD Brain; it does nothing until you sign in.

summary: Sets up a Getting Things Done vault (Inbox, contexts, Projects, Waiting For, Someday Maybe) and two-way syncs its notes with a GTD Brain board.
